newsitem.title: USA: Board says 19 Illinois counties to vote on tax cap.
newsitem.headline: Board says 19 Illinois counties to vote on tax cap.

text.p: A final accounting by the Illinois Board of Elections showed 19 Illinois counties will have a tax cap measure on their November 5 ballot.
A preliminary accounting by the elections board last week indicated that voters in 20 Illinois counties would decide whether they want limitations on property tax increases.
However, McLean County opted for an April election instead, according to the elections board.
Under a measure passed by the General Assembly in May, county boards in 96 counties outside of the Chicago area were eligible to place a tax cap referendum on the ballot.

Tax caps are already in place in six Chicago area counties where they limit annual increases in local property tax collections to five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. The restriction also prohibits the issuance of general obligation debt without voter approval.

Illinois counties that will vote on tax caps in November are Boone, Champaign, Christian, Franklin, Jackson, Kankakee, Lee, Logan, Macoupin, Massac, Menard, Monroe, Morgan, Randolph, Sangamon, Schuyler, Union, Williamson and Winnebago.
